title: How does the sum change when one term changes?
description: Starting from one known sum, four nearby sums are found by asking whether a term went up or down, with no adding afresh. Keeko's doubt is that minus fifteen is smaller than minus sixteen, so the sum goes down.
teaching_notes: One idea: a sum goes up by as much as one term goes up, and down by as much as one term goes down. Ask the child to place minus fifteen and minus sixteen on a number line.

video_script.why: The child sees four new sums found from one known sum by asking whether a term went up or down.
video_script.substitution: Change the numbers and the method stays the same: a term one more makes the sum one more, a term one less makes it one less.
video_script.anchor: the known sum 53 plus minus 16 equals 37, with a number line below it
video_script.wrong_answer: minus fifteen is smaller than minus sixteen, so the sum goes down
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko treats minus fifteen as smaller than minus sixteen because fifteen is less than sixteen, so the sum goes the wrong way.
video_script.payoff_line: The sums are thirty eight, thirty six, thirty eight and thirty six.

final_answer.spoken: thirty eight, thirty six, thirty eight and thirty six

maths_rules: the slip: -15 is greater than -16, not smaller
video_script.design: One idea: the sum moves by as much as a term moves. The known sum and the number line stay in the anchor band; the working band shows each change. Keeko's doubt: minus fifteen is smaller than minus sixteen.
